## Hello,

Thank you for your question. There are two pre-arrival specific communications sent to applicants during the processing of their application:

1. 1. Pre-arrival letter: Sent once the applicant receives a positive eligibility decision, meaning they meet the criteria of the immigration program they are applying to. Depending on the business line, the application final approval can come only a few months after receiving a positive elig8bility decision (e.g. economic immigrants applying via Express Entry) or more than a year later (e.g. Family Class applications).
2. 2. Pre-arrival push notification: Sent between one and two months after applicants receive the pre-arrival letter. It is intended to remind and nudge applicants to register for pre-arrival services.
Thank you,

# Hello,

Thank you for your email correspondence to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.

Question:

On this page [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/study-permits/making-application.htmi](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/study-permits/making-application.htmi), it is written: "Students participating in exchange programs are only eligible to work off campus if they hold a study permit. The processing officer must include the appropriate work authorization conditions when issuing a study permit to exchange students." This clearly stipulate that an exchange student holding a study permit is allowed to work off campus, even if the exchange is less then 6 months.

However, to my knowledge, this authorization to work off campus is not mentioned anywhere else on IRCC websites. Therefore, I would like to have a confirmation if exchange student holding a study permit are allowed to work off campus. If yes, I would like to know if it's mention anywhere else on IRCC websites.

Answer:

Exchange students are students who have been admitted to an institution as visiting students. However, they are not subject to any tuition fees from their host institution, as these fees are covered by an exchange agreement between the host and home institutions. In most cases, exchange students do not require a study permit, since their length of stay is usually less than 6 months. However, they may still apply for a study permit. For programs of 6 months or longer in duration, exchange students must apply for a study permit. Students participating in exchange programs are eligible to work off campus only if they hold a study permit. The processing officer must include the appropriate work authorization conditions when issuing a study permit to exchange students.

While a study permit is not required for short-term courses, an officer must accept and process an application for a study permit, even when the duration of the course or program of study is 6 months or less [R188(2)].

For more information, please visit our website <[https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/study-permits/making-application.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/study-permits/making-application.html)>.

We trust this information will be useful

Sincerely,

The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

Cc: Immigration Representatives / Représentants immigration (IRCC) Subject: TR: Clarification Regarding Common-Law Dependent Eligibility Under CEC-REP-2024-1867 - Due 4-Nov-24 Importance: Normal Sensitivity: None

# Hello,

Thank you for your email correspondence to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.

Question:

This example is based entirely on assumption. If the dependent (Person B) of a principal applicant (Person A) under the Canadian Experience Class (CEC) is married to someone else (Person C), and C is living outside of Canada. Assuming that A and B have been living together in a common-law relationship that has lasted for at least one year. Person B and C are in the process of filing for a divorce, but no court order or divorce certificate has been issued yet, as the

# application is still being processed.

In this assumption, could B be considered a dependent of A based on their common-law relationship, despite Person B still being legally married to Person C?

Answer: A person, who is married to a third party, may be considered a common-law partner (dependent) of a principal applicant, if they meet certain conditions. Persons who are married to third parties may be considered common-law partners provided their marriage has broken down and they have lived separate and apart from their spouse for at least one year, during which time they must have cohabited in a conjugal relationship with the common-law partner. Cohabitation with a common-law partner can only be considered to have stārted once a physical separation from the spouse has occurred. A common-law relationship cannot be legally established if one or both parties continue to maintain a conjugal relationship with a person to whom they remain legally married.

Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.

We trust that this information will assist you.

# Sincerely,

### Good Day,

Thank you for your email correspondence to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.

Question:

Under Express Entry Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS), can Canadian self-employed work experience be considered as foreign work experience for skil transferability points? For your ease of reference, please see below chart excerpted from RCC website: [https://www.canada.ca/enámmigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/eligibility/critenia-comprehensive-ranking-system/grid.html](https://www.canada.ca/enámmigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/eligibility/critenia-comprehensive-ranking-system/grid.html)

Answer.

If you are a resident of Canada and the business activities are taking place in Canada; your work experience in Canada was for a Canadian entity or Canadian business; then it is likely not foreign work experience.

Pursuant to Section 25(1) of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system, for the purposes of sections 23 and 24, foreign work experience is work experience that

(a) is acquired by a foreign national outside Canada in one or more occupations listed in TEER Category 0, 1, 2 or 3 of the National Occupational Classification;

Answer:

MEC must be met both at ITA and APR (application submission date) in order for the application to be considered under the Express Entry, including obtaining the minimum number of hours of work experience. We are aware, however, that some applicants may receive an invitation to apply (ITA) up to a month early, because the system calculates applicants' work experience by months, rounding up, and not by individual hours worked. This calculation is working as intended, and there is no need to decline an iTA or delay submission of an application if the applicant is maintaining their employment.

If the system deems the client ready to be invited, MEC may be considered met, if the applicant entered all information truthfuily and accurately and met ali the other requirements. IRCC officers are aware of this calculation process and will take it into consideration at the time the application is processed.

# Hello,

Thank you for your email correspondence to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada’s Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.

Question:

The inquiry concerns the Canadian Experience Class (CEC) category. Our client is employed as a survey pilot with a Canadian survey company based in Ottawa. The nature of his work requires him to travel frequently outside of Canada for various survey projects. We would like to confirm whether the time he spends working abroad for his Canadian employer would still count towards his Canadian work experience requirements for his permanent residency application under the CEC.

Answer: Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations paragraph 87.1(2)(a) states that work experience must be acquired in Canada to be eligible as entry criteria under the Canadian Experience Class (CEC). Work experience gained for a Canadian employer but outside of Canada is not eligible under this criteria. Work experience gained abroad may be eligible as foreign work experience for Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) points and towards meeting certain selection criteria.

Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.

We trust that this information will assist you.

Sincerely,

## Good Day,

Thank you for your email correspondence to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.

Question:

If an applicant only has self-employed work experience accumulated in Canada, can the Canadian self-employed experience be counted toward the minimum work experience under Federal Skilled Worker Program? If an applicant only has self-employed work experience in Canada, will he/she be disqualified for Federal Skilled Worker Program?

Answer:

There is nothing precluding self-employed work experience in the Federal Skilled Worker (FSW) Class. In order to be assigned the appropriate number of Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) points and to be screened against the minimum entry criteria of the correct program (FSW), please ensure you click the box for “self-employment" next to the declared work experience in your candidate profile. The work experience however, will not count for Canadian work experience CRS points in the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system (Section 15(7) & 19(8)) The definitions outlined here are also applicable for skill transferability. (Section 22(4) & 24(3))

Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis; each application will be considered on its own merits, with a final decision based on a review of all the information available to the officer at the time of decision. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.

We trust that this information will assist you.

Sincerely,

Question: If I understand you correctly, in order to obtain maintained status, an application to extend a study permit must be submitted online through the RCC Secure Account while if the student extends their study permit through IRCC portal, they do not have

#### maintained status. Is my understanding right?

Response: A temporary resident who applied for an extension to their period of authorized stay before it expired (e.g., before their study permit expired [IRPR 181]) is considered to have 'maintained their status' as a temporary resident [IRPR 183(5)] until a

### decision is made on their extension application.

### ●* If their extension application is refused, their maintained status ends on the refusal date.

- * If their extension application is approved, their stay continues to be authorized until the extension's expiry date.
In-Canada holders of valid study permits are directed to apply to extend their study permit via the IRCC Secure Account. In some cases, applicants may be eligible for an exemption that allows them to apply on paper.

If you're applying for a study permit extension

Use the IRCC secure account when you apply to extend your study permit. Even if you applied for your initial study permit using another account, you must use the secure account when you apply to extend your study permit.

Applicants wishing to check if their application was received by IRCC, or to check the status of their application, should refer to our website:

Good Morning, The IRCC online portals are not just for outside-Canada applications, they are also used for online temporary and permanent residence application intake. There are different types of portals, such as the Authorized Representative Portal, the IRCC Portal, the PR Portal, and the IRCC Secure Account. More information on the different portals, as well as how to confirm which portal is the correct one for a specific application type, can be found here: Sign in: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada accounts-Canada.ca In order to obtain maintained status, an application to extend a study permit must be submitted online through the IRCC

# Secure Account:

Foreign nationals who are in Canada as temporary residents and are seeking to extend their temporary resident status or their authorization to work or study must apply by electronic means only, unless otherwise specified. On June 4, 2019, the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) were amended to make an electronic application mandatory for most temporary residence applications made from within Canada. Specifically, section R9.2 provides that the following applications must be made by the electronic means made available or specified by the Minister for that purpose:

- an application for an extension of an authorization to remain in Canada as a temporary resident
- an application that is made in Canada for a work or study permit or for renewal of such a permit
- an application for the restoration of temporary resident status
- an application that is made pursuant to a youth mobility arrangement entered into by Canada
Therefore, the study permit extension application must be submitted online in advance of the expiry date on the current study permit for maintained status to begin while the extension application processes. For more information on study permit extensions, please see here: Extend your study permit or restore your status: How to apply-Canada.ca.

# Hello,

Thank you for your email correspondence to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's Immigration Representatives mailbox. Please consider that the Immigration Representatives Mailbox will only reply to general immigration program or policy related enquiries; therefore, no case-specific responses can be provided.

We appreciate your patience. Please see below:

Maintained status is an extension of the period of authorized stay as a temporary resident if they have applied to extend their period of authorized stay before it ends. As indicated in our operational instructions and guidelines, the date and time of receipt are important for determining if status is maintained under subsection R183(5). For electronic applications, the department uses Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) around the world to ensure that time is equal for all. Therefore, receipt dates and times do not depend on time zones; all applications must be submitted before midnight UTC on the date the applicant's status expires. If the application was received after midnight UTC on the date of expiry, the applicant does not maintain their status under subsection R183(5).

This means that to benefit from maintained status, an electronic application must be received in the system, regardless of the system used.

We trust this information will be useful.

# Hello,

Thank you for your email correspondence to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's Immigration Representatives mailbox. Please consider that the Immigration Representatives Mailbox will only reply to general immigration program- or policy-related enquiries; therefore, no case-specific responses can be provided.

We appreciate your patience. Please find the answers to your questions below:

1. 1. If spring/summer is a student's final semester, they can only work up to 20 hours right? Response: They must be a full-time student both before and after a regularly scheduled break to work full-time during the break. In this situation they can only work up to 20 hours per week during the break. If the spring/summer period is not a regularly scheduled break, then students authorized to work off-campus can only do so up to 20 hours per week.
2. 2. If a deferral is approved by the school and they issued a new letter of acceptance, can the student come to Canada with their previous IRCC letter of introduction which is still valid? Response: To enter Canada, they must have a valid port of entry letter of introduction from IRCC and the original and updated letter of acceptance from the same DLI. As long as they will be attending the same DLl, they do not need to reapply for a study permit. If a student changes their program of study to a different DLl after their visa is issued, they need to submit a new study permit application to IRCC. Students should immediately submit their new LOA to IRCC using the online web form if they made any changes to their program of study within the same DLl or to a different DLI while their study permit application is still in process.
3. 3. I got the information from IRCC before that "Please note that the passport number indicated on your document has no impact on the information related to your current status." Do they have to apply for a new study permit after they get their new passport? Response: We apologize for the misunderstanding in our previous response. If they have a new passport, they do not need to change their study permit until it expires.
4. 4. Given it is a new application for IRCC portal application instead of study permit extension, do they have maintained status? Response: Regardless of the system used, if IRCC received a complete application before the expiry date of their previous document, they would have maintained status until a decision is made on the new application. If the applicant hasn't received an AOR letter, they will need to submit a new application and pay the fees.
5. 5. Does it mean that IRCC portal application does not grant maintained status? Response: Maintained status is only extended under R183(5) if IRCC receives a complete application before the period of authorized stay ends. If the applicant is not aware that IRCC has received a complete application, and their study permit has expired, they will need to apply to restore their status.
We trust this information will be useful.

If the student has both a study permit and an Iranian open work permit, can they study full time and work full time at the same time? Response: The person would have to abide by the conditions of their study permit, which include being enrolled at a DLl and actively pursuing their studies. Actively pursuing their studies means

- * being enrolled full-time or part-time during each academic semester (excluding regularly scheduled breaks)
- * making progress towards completing their program's courses, and
* not taking authorized leave longer than 150 days from their study program
An open work permit holder may work part- or full-time until the expiry date of that work permit.

(2) Spring/summer is the student's scheduled break. However, this the spring/summer is the student's final semester, how many hours can they work by using their study permit?
Response: Students eligible to work without a work permit under paragraph R186(v) can do the following:

- * work up to 20 hours per week during academic sessions once they have commenced their program of study
- * work full time during regularly scheduled breaks between academic sessions regardless of their course load

(3)The student has their study permit approved for Fall 2023 by using the offer of admission for Fall 2023. Their letter of introduction is still valid. They deferred their program start from Fall 2023 to Fall 2024 after their study permit's approval. Can they use their letter of introduction to come to Canada with their updated offer of admission? Do they need to apply for a new study permit?
Response: If the student defers their program start date, it should be formally approved by the DLI. In all deferral cases, students should obtain an updated letter of acceptance from the DLl. To enter Canada, they must have the port of entry letter of introduction from IRCC and a copy of a valid letter of acceptance from their school. If the letter of acceptance is not valid, they would need to apply for a new study permit.

(4) If the student loses their passport but they did not lose their study permit, can they continue using that study permit with the lost passport number?
Response: They will need to apply for a new passport through their country's consulate or embassy and then apply for a new study permit which will reflect the new passport number.

(5) A) If the student mistakenly uses the IRCC portal instead of IRCC secure account for their study permit extension, will they have maintained status by using IRCC portal?
Response: In order to have maintained status IRCC must have received a complete application before midnight UTC on the date the applicant's status expires. If the application was received after midnight UTC on the date of expiry, the applicant does not maintain their status under subsection R183(5).

If IRCC received a complete application, the applicant would have received an acknowledgement of receipt (AOR) letter (or email). If they haven't received a AOR letter, they will have to submit an application to restore their status and they are not able to continue under the conditions of their expired study permit (they can't study, nor work on or off campus). They have 90 days to apply for restoration of status from the date the study permit expired. If more than 90 days have passed, they will have to leave Canada or reapply from outside Canada for a new study permit.

It is important to note that the IRCC secure account is used to extend a study permit while the IRCC portal is for a new application. Since a provincial attestation letter (PAL) is now required for new study permit applications, the student will not be able to proceed in using the IRCC portal for an extension because they won't have a PAL. They will need to submit a new application.
